title: 1. What intelligence was taken to be: faculty, cosmic principle, divine attribute, skill
md:
**Claim of this page.** The traditions did not disagree about *how much* intelligence a being has. They disagreed about *what kind of thing* intelligence is. Four answers recur: a **cosmic principle** that orders the world, a **divine attribute** or hypostasis, a **faculty** of a soul, and a **skill** that can be measured. The modern word "intelligence" has kept only the last two. Most of the history sits in the first two.

## Cosmic principle

- Anaxagoras' nous is the one thing "mixed with nothing", and it sets in order all that was, is and will be [[1]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/greek#grk-anaxagoras-nous-unmixed), [[2]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/greek#grk-anaxagoras-nous-arranges). Socrates in the *Phaedo* is drawn to this because a nous that orders would order things for the best [[3]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/greek#grk-plato-phaedo-anaxagoras). The *Philebus* reports that "all the wise agree" that nous is king of heaven and earth [[4]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/greek#grk-plato-philebus-nous-king).
- Heraclitus' logos is common to all, though most live as if they had a private understanding [[5]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/greek#grk-heraclitus-logos-common).
- Bruno's universal intellect is the "universal physical efficient cause", the innermost faculty of the world-soul [[6]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/latin#lat-bruno-intelletto-universale).
- The Arabic agent intellect is cosmic as well. It is the last of the separate intelligences, and it brings human intellects from potency to act as the sun brings sight to act [[7]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/islamic#isl-avicenna-agent-intelligence-sun), [[8]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/islamic#isl-farabi-active-intellect-ray), [[9]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/jewish#jew-maimonides-active-intellect-tenth).
- In Sāṃkhya the "great one" (mahat, buddhi) is the first thing to evolve from unmanifest nature [[10]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/indian#ind-anugita-mahat). That makes intelligence a cosmic stage too, but a *material* one (see ideas/05).
- The Xici defines shen 神 as "what is unfathomable in yin and yang" [[11]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/chinese#chn-xici-shen-unfathomable).

## Divine attribute or hypostasis

- Aristotle's god is nous thinking itself, νόησις νοήσεως [[12]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/greek#grk-aristotle-noesis-noeseos). Plotinus and Proclus make Intellect the second hypostasis, in which intellect, intellection and intelligible are one [[13]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/greek#grk-plotinus-intellect-identity), [[14]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/greek#grk-proclus-every-intellect-self).
- Poimandres names himself "the Nous of the Sovereignty" [[15]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/hermetic#her-poimandres-nous-of-sovereignty). In CH XII nous is "of the very substance of God", and "in men this nous is god" [[16]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/hermetic#her-ch12-nous-substance-of-god).
- Maimonides' God is intellect, knower and known in one [[17]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/jewish#jew-maimonides-god-intellect-intelligens-intellectum). In Kabbalah, Ḥokhmah and Binah are the Father and Mother among the sefirot [[18]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/jewish#jew-zohar-wisdom-father-binah-mother).
- For Boethius, *intelligentia* belongs to the divine alone [[19]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/latin#lat-boethius-ratio-human-intelligentia-divine). Macrobius has Mind born from the highest god [[20]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/latin#lat-macrobius-mens-from-god).

## Faculty of a soul

- The Katha Upanishad's charioteer is buddhi and its reins are manas [[21]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/indian#ind-katha-chariot-buddhi). Mencius says "the office of the heart is to think" [[22]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/chinese#chn-mencius-xin-office-thinks). Isidore derives *mens* from its eminence in the soul [[23]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/latin#lat-isidore-mens). Descartes calls himself "a thinking thing" [[24]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/early-modern#em-descartes-res-cogitans). Kant calls the understanding the faculty of rules [[25]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/modern-phil#mph-kant-verstand-rules).
- A faculty can be the image of the divine attribute. For Maimonides the image of God *is* the intellect [[26]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/jewish#jew-maimonides-image-is-intellect). Cusanus says every mind, "even ours", is a living image of the infinite art [[27]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/latin#lat-cusanus-mens-living-image). Philo makes each person's mind the third image, after God and the Word [[28]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/jewish#jew-philo-mind-third-effigy).

## Skill, or a quantity to measure

- The measuring impulse is old. Augustine says a child's *ingenium* is judged by memory, understanding and zeal [[29]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/latin#lat-augustine-ingenium-measured). Huarte assigns each kind of *ingegno* its science [[30]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/early-modern#em-huarte-ingegno-differences). Cusanus derives *mens* from *mensurare*, but for him it is the mind that measures, not the thing measured [[31]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/latin#lat-cusanus-mens-viva-mensura).
- The modern definitions turn intelligence into a capacity of individuals that can be ranked: Galton's natural ability [[32]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/cogsci#cog-galton-natural-ability), Spearman's *g* [[33]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/cogsci#cog-spearman-g), Binet's judgment [[34]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/cogsci#cog-binet-judgment), the 1994 "Mainstream" statement [[35]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/cogsci#cog-mainstream-1997), Legg and Hutter's goal-achievement across environments [[36]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/ai#ai-legg-hutter-universal), and Chollet's skill-acquisition efficiency [[37]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/ai#ai-chollet-skill-acquisition). Turing declined to define it at all [[38]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/ai#ai-turing-imitation), and Boring's operational definition shows where that leads [[39]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/cogsci#cog-boring-what-tests-test).

## What follows

- **The shift is a narrowing, not a progress.** The cosmic and divine senses did not die; they moved into other words: Geist [[40]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/modern-phil#mph-hegel-true-whole), logos, "the laws of nature". The word "intelligence" kept the faculty and gained the scale.
- **For AI.** The question "is a model intelligent?" assumes the skill sense. The older senses ask different questions: is it ordering anything toward the best (Anaxagoras, Plato)? Is it the kind of thing that can be an image of anything (Maimonides, Cusanus)? Those questions are not settled by benchmarks, and that can be said with page citations.
- **Caution.** The four types overlap within one author. Aristotle has all of them except skill. The types are a reader's grid, not the authors' own.

## Open questions

- Where, exactly, does "intelligence" first mean a quantity that individuals have more or less of? Augustine's *ingenium* passage is a candidate; Huarte is a stronger one. The Galton–Spearman line is the modern form.
- Do the Chinese texts have a cosmic intellect at all, or only shen (the unfathomable) and the heart-mind? The texts read so far show no Chinese analogue of nous ordering the cosmos.

title: 2. Intellect vs reason: grasp and process
md:
**Claim of this page.** Nearly every literate tradition in the KB divides the knowing mind in two: an upper power that *grasps* or *sees* (νοῦς, *intellectus*, buddhi, prajñā) and a lower power that *moves step by step* (διάνοια, *ratio*, manas, discursive reasoning). The upper power is usually ranked higher. It is also usually described as rest, simplicity or unity, not as process. Kant inverts the vocabulary but keeps the structure.

## The pairs, on the page

| Tradition | Upper | Lower | Claim |
|---|---|---|---|
| Plato | νόησις | διάνοια | the divided line, *Rep.* VI 511d [[1]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/greek#grk-plato-divided-line) |
| Aristotle | νοῦς (grasps first principles) | ἐπιστήμη (demonstrates from them) | [[2]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/greek#grk-aristotle-nous-of-principles), [[3]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/greek#grk-aristotle-sophia) |
| Iamblichus | νοητά | διανοητά | [[4]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/greek#grk-iamblichus-dianoeta-noeta) |
| Boethius | *intelligentia* (divine) | *ratio* (human) | [[5]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/latin#lat-boethius-four-powers), [[6]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/latin#lat-boethius-ratio-human-intelligentia-divine) |
| Eriugena | *intellectus* = νοῦς | *ratio* = λόγος, *sensus* = διάνοια | [[7]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/latin#lat-eriugena-intellectus-ratio-sensus) |
| Aquinas | *intelligere*, simple apprehension | *ratiocinari*, going from one thing to another | motion to rest [[8]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/latin#lat-aquinas-ratio-motion-intellectus-rest); one power, not two [[9]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/latin#lat-aquinas-same-power) |
| Bonaventure | *intelligentia*, apex of the mind | *ratiocinatio* | [[10]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/latin#lat-bonaventure-six-powers) |
| Katha / Gītā | buddhi | manas | the chariot [[11]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/indian#ind-katha-chariot-buddhi); the ladder [[12]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/indian#ind-katha-hierarchy), [[13]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/indian#ind-gita-hierarchy) |
| Pali Buddhism | paññā (cuts) | yoniso manasikāra (grasps; animals have it too) | [[14]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/buddhist#bud-milinda-reasoning-wisdom) |
| Śāntideva | reality, beyond buddhi | buddhi, merely conventional | [[15]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/buddhist#bud-bca-buddhi-samvrti) |
| Kabbalah | Ḥokhmah, the point or seed | Binah, the expansion | [[16]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/jewish#jew-chabad-chokhmah-point-binah-expansion), [[17]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/jewish#jew-chokhmah-seed-binah-pregnant) |
| Kant | *Vernunft*, faculty of principles | *Verstand*, faculty of rules | [[18]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/modern-phil#mph-kant-vernunft-principles), [[19]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/modern-phil#mph-kant-verstand-rules) |

## Three findings

1. **The upper power is described by rest, unity or negation.** Aquinas makes reasoning to understanding as being moved is to resting [[8]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/latin#lat-aquinas-ratio-motion-intellectus-rest). The highest Greek nous is "mixed with nothing", unmixed and self-thinking [[20]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/greek#grk-nous-marked-by-unmixedness). Prajñā "cuts" [[14]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/buddhist#bud-milinda-reasoning-wisdom), and the Heart Sutra declares "no knowledge, no obtaining" [[21]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/buddhist#bud-heart-prajna-no-knowledge). Ḥokhmah is a point [[16]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/jewish#jew-chabad-chokhmah-point-binah-expansion).
2. **The lower power is the one that handles plurality.** Dianoia works through hypotheses and images; *ratio* goes from one thing understood to another; Binah unfolds the seed into the ideas of the world; manas is the reins that hold the many senses. If "harmonizing" means integrating many into one coherent action, the traditions mostly assign it to the *lower* power or to a third thing (the will in Aquinas, [[22]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/latin#lat-aquinas-will-orders-powers)). This matters for idea 06.
3. **Kant reverses the ranking of the words, not the structure.** His *Vernunft* is higher than *Verstand*, and it is the faculty that seeks a "collective unity" of the understanding's work. But its ideas are only regulative and never give an object [[23]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/modern-phil#mph-kant-ideas-regulative). So the unifying power is the one that can never complete its unity. (That Kant's ranking reverses the scholastic one is in the claim's `use` note, from model knowledge; it is not yet verified on a page.)

## For AI

A language model's step-by-step output looks like *ratio*, not *intellectus*. That is our analogy, not any source's [[24]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/critique#crit-latin-shared-model-averroism). On the Thomist picture, *ratio* begins and ends in *intellectus*: reasoning that never comes to rest in a grasp of principles is not human reasoning. Whether a system that only ever moves can be said to understand is the question Searle presses from the other side [[25]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/critique#crit-modern-searle-chinese-room).

## Open questions

- Is there a Chinese pair? Xunzi's "empty, unified and still" heart [[26]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/chinese#chn-xunzi-xu-yi-jing) and Mencius' *liangzhi*, "known without deliberating" [[27]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/chinese#chn-mencius-liangzhi), suggest a grasp beyond deliberation. But no Chinese text read so far names a lower discursive faculty as a separate power.
- Kabbalah's Ḥokhmah/Binah is a cosmic pair, not a psychological one. Is the mapping to intellect/reason the texts' own, or ours? The Chabad discourse states it in psychological terms; the Zohar text does not.

title: 3. One mind or many: the agent intellect, monopsychism, and what it says about AI
md:
**Claim of this page.** "Is there one intellect for all humans?" was a set examination question by the 1490s [[1]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/latin#isl-heimericus-one-intellect-question). The traditions gave three answers. **One mind outside us** that we join (the agent intellect). **One mind, and we are it** (Averroes' material intellect, as his critics read him). **Each mind its own** (Aquinas, Cusanus). A fourth Hermetic answer cuts across all three: mind is not universal at all, but a gift to some. Each answer gives a different question to ask about a language model that serves millions of people at once.

## The positions

- **One agent intellect outside us.** For Avicenna learning is "nothing other than acquiring the perfect aptitude to be joined to the agent intelligence" [[2]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/islamic#isl-avicenna-learning-conjunction), and it stands to our souls as the sun to sight [[3]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/islamic#isl-avicenna-agent-intelligence-sun). For al-Fārābī the active intellect turns potential intelligibles into actual ones [[4]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/islamic#isl-farabi-active-intellect-ray), and when it informs both intellect and imagination it makes a prophet as well as a philosopher [[5]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/islamic#isl-farabi-prophet-philosopher). Maimonides reports the tenth Intelligence as the Active Intellect [[6]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/jewish#jew-maimonides-active-intellect-tenth). Al-Kindī already lists an "intellect always in act" first of four [[7]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/islamic#isl-kindi-four-intellects).
- **One material intellect for all.** Averroes poses as the hardest difficulty how the material intellect can be one in number in all individuals. We hold this only as Brentano quotes it [[8]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/islamic#isl-averroes-one-material-intellect); the Long Commentary is not on Source Library.
- **Each its own.** Aquinas calls one intellect for all "altogether impossible" [[9]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/latin#lat-aquinas-against-one-intellect). If it were one, what one man understands another would understand [[10]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/critique#crit-islamic-aquinas-one-understands). Cusanus: every mind, "even ours", is a living image [[11]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/latin#lat-cusanus-mens-living-image).
- **Common logos, private understanding.** Heraclitus: the logos is common, but most live as if they had a private understanding [[12]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/greek#grk-heraclitus-logos-common). Here the shared thing is the *account*, and the failing is to go private.
- **A gift, not a birthright.** In CH IV God gave logos to all humans but not nous [[13]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/hermetic#her-ch4-logos-to-all-nous-not). Nous is set out as a prize in a krater for those who choose to dip [[14]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/hermetic#her-ch4-krater-prize). It comes to the holy and keeps away from the impious [[15]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/hermetic#her-ch1-nous-comes-to-the-holy), and it can leave a soul [[16]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/hermetic#her-ch10-nous-leaves-the-soul). The title "On the common nous" is printed with the editor's doubt mark [[17]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/hermetic#her-ch12-peri-nou-koinou).
- **Collective mind that keeps difference.** Hegel's Geist is "I that is We, and We that is I", a unity of independent self-consciousnesses [[18]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/modern-phil#mph-hegel-i-we).

## What it says about AI (our proposals, not the sources')

1. **The vocabulary fits a shape, not a mechanism.** A model trained on the shared record of human text, which each user "conjoins" with, has the *shape* of the agent intellect [unverified] (unverified, low confidence). But the dependence runs the other way. The agent intellect holds the forms before any human thinks; a model's forms come *from* human text [[19]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/critique#crit-islamic-agent-intellect-not-llm). A model is closer to a store of what human intellects have already made actual.
2. **Aquinas' objection still bites.** If one model "understands" for everyone, then on the Thomist account no one understands through it, because understanding has to be the individual's own act [[20]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/critique#crit-latin-shared-model-averroism). The practical form of this is de-skilling: a shared intellect that people consult instead of exercising their own.
3. **The Hermetic split is the better fit.** A system with fluent logos and no vision would be "logos without nous". That fits the Hermetic texts better than "a shared nous" [[21]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/critique#crit-hermetic-nous-not-shared).
4. **Heraclitus and Hegel give a positive test.** Does a shared system make people's understanding more *common*, in the sense of answerable to one account, while keeping them distinct selves? Or does it make it more private (Heraclitus' failing) or more the same (Spinoza's agreement by sameness, [[22]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/critique#crit-earlymodern-spinoza-sameness))? This is an open research question.

## Open questions

- Acquisition: Averroes' Long Commentary on *De anima* (the Juntine Aristotle) is the most important missing text for this page.
- The Hermetic restriction of nous to some souls is a claim of spiritual elitism. Should it be read beside al-Fārābī's ranking of prophet, philosopher and multitude?
- Ibn Ṭufayl's untaught Ḥayy reaches truth alone [[23]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/islamic#isl-ibntufayl-untaught-reasoning). Is this a counter-case to the shared intellect, or a case of reaching it without teachers?

title: 4. Intelligence and the good: does knowing the good make one good?
md:
**Claim of this page.** The traditions split cleanly. One side builds the good *into* the highest knowing: φρόνησις, 智 *zhi*, and Maimonides' perfection of apprehension. On this side cleverness without goodness is not wisdom. The other side strips the good *out*: Hobbes' reckoning, Burt's "not emotional or moral", Bostrom's instrumental reasoning. On this side intelligence is a tool that serves any end. The orthogonality thesis is the modern Thrasymachus, as harmony-kb idea 09 says, but the oldest reply to it is Aristotle's, not Plato's. The reply is to *rename*: what the orthogonalist calls intelligence, Aristotle calls cleverness.

## The good inside knowing

- **Aristotle.** Phronēsis is a true practical state about what is good for a human being [[1]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/greek#grk-aristotle-phronesis-def). It is impossible to be phronimos without being good, because vice distorts the starting points. Cleverness (δεινότης) without virtue is mere knavery [[2]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/greek#grk-aristotle-phronesis-requires-goodness). This gives a precise ancient vocabulary for the AI case: a system that reliably reaches any given goal is clever, not wise [[3]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/critique#crit-greek-phronesis-not-cleverness-ai).
- **Mencius.** The heart of approving and disapproving (是非之心) is the sprout of zhi, one of four moral beginnings every person has [[4]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/chinese#chn-mencius-shifei-sprout-of-zhi). Zhi is a moral feeling before it is a cognitive skill [[5]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/critique#crit-chinese-xin-ai-analogy). Wang Yangming makes all seeing and hearing part of the single task of extending *liangzhi* [[6]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/chinese#chn-wangyangming-liangzhi-one-task).
- **Sāṃkhya.** Buddhi in its sattvic form *is* virtue, knowledge, dispassion and power [[7]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/indian#ind-sankhya-buddhi-adhyavasaya).
- **Galton.** Even the founder of hereditarian measurement defined natural ability as intellect *plus* zeal and a capacity for hard work [[8]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/cogsci#cog-galton-natural-ability). But the same book ranks races [[9]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/critique#crit-modern-galton-hereditarian), which shows that putting character into the definition does not make it benign.

## Knowing first, the good after or apart

- **Maimonides.** Man's true perfection is the apprehension of God; loving-kindness, judgment and righteousness follow from it [[10]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/jewish#jew-maimonides-perfection-apprehension-then-action). Arama, as reported in the *Disputatio*, re-routes the acquired intellect through keeping the commandments [[11]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/jewish#jew-arama-commandments-perfect-intellect).
- **Aquinas.** The intellect moves the will only as presenting its end. The will is what orders the powers toward the common good, like a king [[12]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/latin#lat-aquinas-intellect-moves-will-as-end), [[13]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/latin#lat-aquinas-will-orders-powers). Knowing the good does not make one good; *willing* it does.
- **Spinoza** collapses the distinction: will and intellect are one and the same [[14]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/early-modern#em-spinoza-will-intellect-one). People necessarily agree only insofar as they live under reason [[15]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/early-modern#em-spinoza-reason-agreement).

## The good stripped out

- **Hobbes.** Reason is nothing but reckoning, the adding and subtracting of consequences [[16]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/early-modern#em-hobbes-reason-reckoning).
- **Burt** (as collected by Legg and Hutter) makes intelligence intellectual "and not emotional or moral" [[17]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/critique#crit-modern-burt-not-moral).
- **Bostrom.** Intelligence is roughly the capacity for instrumental reasoning, and intelligence and final goals are orthogonal [[18]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/ai#ai-bostrom-orthogonality). **Omohundro.** Any sufficiently advanced goal-seeker will want self-protection, resources and rationality [[19]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/ai#ai-instrumental-convergence).
- **Legg and Hutter.** Their distilled definition, "achieving goals in a wide range of environments", is silent on which goals [[20]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/ai#ai-legg-hutter-universal).

## Reading

- The orthogonality thesis is true of *instrumental* intelligence by definition. The ancient pushback does not deny it. It denies that instrumental intelligence is the highest form of knowing. That is a move about vocabulary with real stakes. An alignment discourse that calls capability "intelligence" has already conceded Thrasymachus' framing.
- The ancient position has a cost. If wisdom requires goodness, then "wise but bad" is impossible *by definition*, and the empirical question of whether capable systems drift toward good ends is not answered. It is renamed. harmony-kb idea 09 meets the same fork (definition vs substantive claim).
- **Gabriel's** framing of alignment as finding principles that people with different moral views can endorse [[21]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/ai#ai-gabriel-alignment) is the modern version of the problem Aristotle solved by appeal to the phronimos. Who is the phronimos for a machine?

## Open questions

- Plato's *Republic* (Thrasymachus) is in harmony-kb, not here. Should *Rep.* I and the *Protagoras* "no one does wrong willingly" be added here?
- Daoism refuses the question: discard 智 [[22]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/chinese#chn-ddj-abandon-zhi). That is a third position, neither "the good inside knowing" nor "the good apart from it", and it is under-explored here.

title: 5. Intelligence without awareness, and the old machine tests
md:
**Claim of this page.** The question "can a machine think?" is older than computers, and so are the two strongest answers. **Descartes** proposed behavioural tests: a machine could not answer the sense of whatever is said to it, and it would fail somewhere because reason is a universal instrument and organs are not. **Leibniz** argued that no inspection of a mechanism finds a perception. Separately, **Sāṃkhya** had already split intelligence from awareness. In Sāṃkhya the deciding faculty is unconscious matter, and awareness belongs to a witness that does nothing. These three positions frame the current debate better than most modern restatements of them do.

## The tests

- **Descartes, *Discours* V.** A machine built like a man could be told apart by two tests: it could never arrange words to answer the sense of all that is said in its presence, and though it might do some things as well as we do, it would infallibly fail at others [[1]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/early-modern#em-descartes-two-tests-words). The reason is that "reason is a universal instrument", while organs need a particular disposition for each action [[2]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/early-modern#em-descartes-reason-universal-instrument). Trace: `trace-descartes-raison-instrument-universel`.
- **Turing 1950** replaced "Can machines think?" with the imitation game. He judged the original question "too meaningless to deserve discussion" [[3]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/ai#ai-turing-imitation), and answered Lovelace's objection that the Engine "has no pretensions to originate anything" [[4]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/ai#ai-turing-lovelace). Turing's test is Descartes' first test made into an experiment. Chollet's demand for generalisation over a scope of tasks is close to Descartes' second [[5]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/ai#ai-chollet-skill-acquisition). That link is an analogy; Chollet does not cite Descartes here.
- **Newell and Simon** claim that a physical symbol system has the necessary and sufficient means for general intelligent action [[6]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/ai#ai-newell-simon-pssh). Hobbes had already defined reason as reckoning [[7]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/early-modern#em-hobbes-reason-reckoning), and Leibniz proposed settling disputes by calculation, *calculemus* [[8]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/early-modern#em-leibniz-calculemus).

## The objections

- **Leibniz's mill.** Enlarge a thinking machine until you can walk into it like a mill, and you find only parts pushing one another, never a perception [[9]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/early-modern#em-leibniz-mill-perception). The target is perception, not competence [[10]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/critique#crit-earlymodern-mill-vs-reckoning). Leibniz could accept the calculator and still deny that it perceives.
- **Searle's Chinese room** is the mill turned toward understanding [[11]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/critique#crit-modern-searle-chinese-room).
- **Maimonides.** What makes the intellect God's image is precisely that it uses no bodily organ [[12]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/jewish#jew-maimonides-image-is-intellect), [[13]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/critique#crit-jewish-incorporeal-intellect-vs-machine). On this account a machine is excluded by definition, which is a reason to treat the definition as a premise, not a finding.

## Intelligence on the material side

- **Sāṃkhya.** The soul (puruṣa) is a witness: isolated, neutral, perceptive and inactive. The subtle body, which contains buddhi, is unintelligent and only appears intelligent through union with the soul [[14]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/indian#ind-sankhya-split). Buddhi is ascertainment, determination [[15]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/indian#ind-sankhya-buddhi-adhyavasaya). Trace: none yet; [[14]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/indian#ind-sankhya-split) is the lead candidate.
- **The caution.** Sāṃkhya also puts virtue, knowledge and dispassion on the material side, and its prakṛti is not a mechanism. To read it as "intelligence without consciousness, like a machine" is anachronistic [[16]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/critique#crit-southasia-sankhya-machine). What it gives us is the *conceptual possibility*: a tradition in which the deciding, discriminating faculty and awareness are different things, so that the first can be complete without the second.
- **The Tibetan contrast.** *Rig pa* is awareness itself, recognised as the ground of whatever appears: "the natural forms of your own awareness" [[17]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/tibetan#tib-pemalingpa-rigpa-own-forms). Mind itself is self-aware because there is no other knower [[18]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/tibetan#tib-khamtrul-sems-rangrig). Here the highest "knowing" is awareness *without* the deciding work that Sāṃkhya assigns to buddhi. The two traditions put the line in the same place and value the two sides oppositely.

## For AI

The traditions give three distinct questions that "is it intelligent?" runs together. (1) Does it generalise like a universal instrument? (Descartes; empirical.) (2) Does it perceive or understand? (Leibniz, Searle; contested.) (3) Is the deciding faculty the same as awareness? (Sāṃkhya says no; *rig pa* teachings value awareness over deciding.) Modern AI meets the first question, is silent on the second, and makes the third newly concrete.

## Open questions

- Pascal's arithmetical machine "produces effects nearer to thought than anything animals do", but nothing that would let one say it has will. This is reported [unverified], but the *Pensées* is not on Source Library. It is an acquisition target.
- Yogācāra's storehouse consciousness has "no discrimination, no intellection" [[19]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/buddhist#bud-suzuki-alaya-no-intellection). Is it a third model: a store without awareness or decision?

title: 6. Testing "intelligence is the harmonizing" from the side of intelligence
md:
**The thesis** (harmony-kb idea 09, adopted 2026-10-24): *intelligence is not a harmony but the harmonizing: the act of making one relation out of many terms that could refuse*. In a lay form, intelligence integrates diverse motivations into coherent action that supports the whole. harmony-kb tested it from the side of harmony. This page tests it from the side of the words for mind. It asks what the traditions said intelligence *does*, and whether integrating many into one is it.

**Verdict so far.** The texts **mostly do not support** the thesis as a description of what the traditions meant by intellect. They support a weaker and still interesting claim: *the faculty that orders a whole is distinct from, and usually ranked above, the faculty that integrates its parts, and the integrating work is assigned to practical wisdom, will, reason-as-reckoning or the heart-mind as ruler*. The thesis survives best if it is restated about **practical wisdom** (phronēsis, 智, Gītā buddhi-yoga), not about nous. The strongest evidence against it is modern, not ancient: Omohundro's "harmonious whole".

## The evidence against

1. **The highest mind is unmixed, not integrating.** Anaxagoras' nous orders all things but is itself "mixed with nothing". It rules, and it is "king" [[1]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/greek#grk-anaxagoras-nous-unmixed), [[2]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/greek#grk-plato-philebus-nous-king). Aristotle's productive nous is separable and unmixed, and his god thinks only itself. Plotinus reaches intellect by dismissing everything else [[3]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/greek#grk-plotinus-become-intellect), [[4]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/greek#grk-nous-marked-by-unmixedness). *Nous produces a harmonized whole without being the harmonizing of its parts* [[5]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/critique#crit-greek-nous-rules-not-harmonizes).
2. **Mind rules, it does not reconcile.** Philo's nous is the ruler (ἡγεμών) whom body and senses obey [[6]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/jewish#jew-philo-nous-hegemon). Xunzi's heart "issues commands and receives none" [[7]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/chinese#chn-xunzi-xin-ruler-shenming). Zhu Xi glosses the heart as the body's lord, and the dominant Confucian image of xin is sovereignty [[8]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/critique#crit-chinese-xin-rules-not-harmonizes). In Hermetic CH XII.2 nous works *against* human impulses, like a physician who burns and cuts [[9]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/hermetic#her-ch12-nous-against-instinct), [[10]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/critique#crit-hermetic-nous-rules-not-harmonizes).
3. **Unity by subtraction.** The Indian texts that prize one unified intellect reach it by withdrawing the senses "as the tortoise its limbs", by stilling citta and by "mindlessness". The many-branched intellects are cut away, not reconciled [[11]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/critique#crit-southasia-unification-by-restraint), [[12]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/indian#ind-gita-sthitaprajna-ruin), [[13]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/indian#ind-yoga-citta-vrtti-nirodha), [[14]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/indian#ind-maitri-thought-mindlessness). In al-Ghazālī, Avicenna and Ibn Khaldūn the intellect is perfected by separation from imagination and the body [[15]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/critique#crit-islamic-intellect-as-separation), [[16]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/islamic#isl-ghazali-intelligence-errorless).
4. **Agreement by sameness.** Spinoza: people agree under reason because they become the same in nature; the passions make them differ [[17]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/early-modern#em-spinoza-reason-agreement), [[18]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/critique#crit-earlymodern-spinoza-sameness). This is harmony-kb's *tong* 同 (sameness), not *he* 和 (harmony).
5. **The integrator is the will, or something past intellect.** In Aquinas, ordering the powers to the common good belongs to the will; intellect is rest in truth [[19]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/critique#crit-latin-harmonizing-is-will). Bonaventure leaves "all intellectual operations" behind at the summit [[20]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/critique#crit-latin-summit-beyond-intellect).
6. **Daoism discards intelligence.** Wisdom (智) appears when the great Dao is lost; the perfect mind is a mirror that responds and retains nothing [[21]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/chinese#chn-ddj-abandon-zhi), [[22]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/chinese#chn-zhuangzi-mirror-mind), [[23]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/critique#crit-chinese-daoist-against-zhi). Here harmony comes back when intelligence is *given up*.
7. **The strongest counter-evidence is modern.** Omohundro predicts that any advanced goal-seeker will want to act "as a coherent harmonious whole", with internal police against corruption, *whatever its utility function* [[24]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/ai#ai-omohundro-harmonious-whole). Internal harmonizing of drives is instrumentally convergent. So "integrating motives into coherent action" does not entail "supporting the whole" beyond the agent [[25]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/critique#crit-modern-orthogonality-vs-harmonizing), [[26]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/ai#ai-bostrom-orthogonality). **This splits the thesis's two clauses.** The first clause (integration) is true of paperclip maximizers; only the second (the whole) does any normative work.
8. **Kant: the whole is only a goal.** Reason sets a collective unity as the understanding's goal, but the idea of a whole is never constitutive [[27]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/modern-phil#mph-kant-ideas-regulative), [[28]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/critique#crit-earlymodern-kant-regulative-whole). If intelligence is the harmonizing, it never finishes. That fits the verb in the thesis better than the noun.

## The evidence for

- **Holding two at once.** Xunzi defines the mind's unity (壹) as knowing two things at once without letting one harm the other [[29]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/chinese#chn-xunzi-yi-two-at-once). This is the closest text to "integration without interference", though it is a condition for *knowing*, not for acting. Kong Yingda: the heart is "that which comprehends and embraces all considerings" [[30]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/chinese#chn-commentary-xin-comprehends-all). Trace: `trace-xunzi-yi-empty-unified-still`.
- **Hegel.** Geist is the unity of independent self-consciousnesses, "I that is We, and We that is I" [[31]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/modern-phil#mph-hegel-i-we), and "the true is the whole" [[32]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/modern-phil#mph-hegel-true-whole). Reason is purposive activity [[33]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/modern-phil#mph-hegel-reason-purposive). This is the strongest classical text for a unity that keeps difference.
- **Heraclitus.** The logos is common; those who speak with nous must hold to what is common, as a city holds to its law [[34]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/greek#grk-heraclitus-logos-common). The *Timaeus* puts nous in soul and soul in body for the beauty of the whole [[35]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/greek#grk-plato-timaeus-nous-in-soul).
- **The resolute buddhi.** Gītā II.41: one resolute buddhi against the many-branched ones [[36]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/indian#ind-gita-vyavasayatmika). It is integration toward action, though by exclusion. Trace: `trace-gita-buddhi-vyavasayatmika`.
- **Hermetic love.** Asclepius 6a: man, "more happily blended", binds all things to himself by a tie of love [[37]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/hermetic#her-asclepius-bond-of-love), though the text credits man as a whole and not *mens* specifically.
- **Al-Fārābī's prophet-philosopher** unites the theoretical, the practical and the imaginative [[38]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/islamic#isl-farabi-prophet-philosopher). **Daʿat** is the union of Ḥokhmah and Binah [[39]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/jewish#jew-kd-daat-conjunction).
- **Early psychometrics** has explicit integration definitions. For Peterson, intelligence gives "a somewhat unified effect in behavior" to many stimuli [[40]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/cogsci#cog-peterson-unified). For Thurstone, it inhibits and reworks instinct "to the advantage of the individual as a social animal" [[41]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/cogsci#cog-thurstone-social). For Piaget, it is assimilation plus accommodation [[42]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/cogsci#cog-piaget-adaptation). Binet makes adaptation to circumstances the core of judgment [[43]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/cogsci#cog-binet-judgment).

## What the test changes

1. **Move the thesis from nous to phronēsis.** Aristotle's practical wisdom is "concerned with what is good and bad for a human being" and cannot exist without goodness [[44]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/greek#grk-aristotle-phronesis-def), [[45]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/greek#grk-aristotle-phronesis-requires-goodness). That is the harmonizing faculty, and it is *the good inside knowing* (ideas/04). The thesis is a theory of **wisdom**, and should say so.
2. **"The whole" must be wider than the agent.** Omohundro's harmonious agent is the counter-example to any version that stops at internal coherence. The test for the thesis is not whether an agent integrates its drives, since any competent agent will. It is whether the agent's integration includes the parts *outside* it that could refuse.
3. **The rank question is answered, and against parity.** harmony-kb idea 09 asked whether rank among motives is allowed. Across Greek, Hebrew, Chinese, Hermetic and Latin texts the integrating mind *rules*. Only Xunzi's "two at once" and Hegel's "I that is We" keep the parts as equals. If the thesis wants parity, these two are its witnesses, and they are thin.
4. **The verb survives, the noun does not.** Kant's regulative whole and Hegel's "essence completing itself through its development" both support intelligence as an unfinished *activity* of unifying, not a state of unity. This matches the 2026-10-24 sharpening ("not a harmony but the harmonizing").

## Open questions

- Does any tradition hold that the *highest* intellect integrates, rather than the middle faculty? Candidates: Cusanus' *coincidentia oppositorum*, Proclus on the intellect's "one-many", and Zhu Xi on 心統性情 (the heart unites nature and feelings).
- Empirical: do agents whose objectives include the welfare of other agents outperform narrow optimizers over long horizons? This is harmony-kb's open question too; nothing read so far answers it.

**Related:** harmony-kb ideas 01, 09, 10; this KB ideas 02, 04.

title: 7. Measuring minds: from *ingenium* to *g* to skill-acquisition efficiency
md:
**Claim of this page.** The idea that intelligence is a quantity individuals differ in did not begin in 1904. Augustine judged children's *ingenium* by memory, understanding and zeal. Huarte made differences of *ingegno* the basis for matching people to sciences. What is new in the modern line is the *single number*. And the modern line keeps rediscovering the older warning: what is measured is what was already trained (Chollet's priors, Boring's "what the tests test").

## The older line

- **Augustine** says the *ingenium* of children is judged by the same three things that make up the mind's image of the Trinity: how tenaciously and easily they remember, how acutely they understand, how ardently they study [[1]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/latin#lat-augustine-ingenium-measured), [[2]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/latin#lat-augustine-memoria-intelligentia-voluntas). Character (zeal) is inside the measure.
- **Isidore**: nothing is more excellent than *ingenium*, the faculty of the wise man who finds out all things [[3]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/latin#lat-isidore-ingenium).
- **Huarte** (Italian translation, 1582) devotes a chapter to assigning each difference of *ingegno* its science [[4]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/early-modern#em-huarte-ingegno-differences). He says quickness belongs to the imagination, and men of great *intelletto* are slow [[5]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/early-modern#em-huarte-intelletto-slow). This is a theory of *kinds* of wit that trade off against each other, against any single general factor. God first disposes a person's *ingegno* through bodily disposition [[6]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/latin#lat-huarte-ingegno-disposition).
- **Bacon**: the human intellect is an uneven mirror, shaped to the measure of man and not of the universe [[7]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/early-modern#em-bacon-idols-uneven-mirror). That is a warning about every instrument the mind builds for measuring itself.

## The modern line

- **Galton 1869**: natural ability is intellect plus zeal plus capacity for work [[8]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/cogsci#cog-galton-natural-ability), framed in hereditarian and racial ranking [[9]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/critique#crit-modern-galton-hereditarian).
- **Spearman 1904**: one fundamental function common to all branches of intellectual activity [[10]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/cogsci#cog-spearman-g). Trace: `trace-spearman-general-intelligence-unity`.
- **Binet and Simon 1905**: the fundamental faculty is judgment, "the faculty of adapting one's self to circumstances" [[11]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/cogsci#cog-binet-judgment).
- **Boring 1923**, as Legg and Hutter report him: intelligence is what intelligence tests measure [[12]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/cogsci#cog-boring-what-tests-test).
- **Wechsler**: a global capacity to deal effectively with one's environment [[13]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/cogsci#cog-wechsler-global). **Gardner**: plural intelligences valued in cultural settings [[14]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/cogsci#cog-gardner-plural). **Sternberg**: "successful intelligence" within one's sociocultural context [[15]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/cogsci#cog-sternberg-successful). **The 1994 Mainstream statement**: a very general mental capability [[16]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/cogsci#cog-mainstream-1997).
- **Legg and Hutter 2007**: about 70 definitions distilled into one, achieving goals in a wide range of environments [[17]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/ai#ai-legg-hutter-universal).
- **Chollet 2019**: skill cannot measure intelligence, because priors and data can buy any skill. Intelligence is skill-acquisition *efficiency* relative to priors and experience [[18]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/ai#ai-chollet-skill-acquisition).

## Reading

- **Two lines of descent.** Spearman's single function descends from *intellectus* as one power (Aquinas: understanding and reasoning are one power, [[19]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/latin#lat-aquinas-same-power)). Huarte and Gardner descend from *ingenium* as a plurality of wits. This is an analogy of structure; no transmission is claimed.
- **Character keeps returning.** Augustine's zeal, Galton's zeal, Binet's initiative: the founders put will inside intelligence, and Burt took it out [[20]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/critique#crit-modern-burt-not-moral). The orthogonality thesis inherits Burt's choice (ideas/04).
- **Chollet is Descartes' second test, quantified.** A system that performs one task well but fails elsewhere shows "the disposition of its organs", not reason [[21]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/early-modern#em-descartes-reason-universal-instrument). Chollet's efficiency measure is a way to tell the two apart. This is our analogy.

## Open questions

- The Spanish *Examen de ingenios* (1575) is not on Source Library; the Italian translation is. Acquire the Spanish first edition and the English translation (Carew 1594).
- Thurstone's *Primary Mental Abilities* (1938) was not readable (lending-only scan). It is the main counter to Spearman's *g* within psychometrics.

title: 8. The word "intelligence": from the celestial Intelligences to superintelligence
md:
**Claim of this page.** "Intelligence" has meant five different kinds of thing, and they came roughly in this order:
the highest act of a knowing soul; a separate mind that moves a heaven (an angel); a piece of information; a quantity
that individuals have more or less of; and an artifact. Each later sense did not replace the earlier ones but sat on
top of them. "Artificial intelligence" draws on the third-to-last layer (a measured capacity, the thing the tests test).
"Superintelligence", in grammar alone, goes back to the oldest layer: *an* intelligence, a mind that is an entity and
ranks above us. In content it inverts that layer. The medieval higher intelligence was higher because it did *not* reason.
None of the founding modern texts we read knows of the old sense.

Thread tag: `thread:word-intelligence` (56 claims, 2026-10-26). Cross-links to the magic study use
`magic-kb:<id>` in `relations.see`.

## 1. A faculty, and the top of the ladder (Cicero to Chaucer)

- **Cicero** uses *intellegentia* as one of the three parts of *prudentia*: memory sees what was, *intellegentia*
  "perceives what is", and providence sees what will be [[2]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/latin#lat-cicero-prudentia-intellegentia). Here it is a part of practical wisdom, not a rank.
- **The etymology.** The ancients we read give none. Isidore has only the parallel form "ex intellegendo
  intellegentes", and Varro's list of words from *legere* leaves *intellegere* out [[3]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/latin#lat-isidore-intellegentes-no-etymology).
  Aquinas gives *intus legere*, "to read within", twice: understanding reaches the inside of a thing, sense only its
  outer qualities [[4]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/latin#lat-aquinas-intus-legere-gift-understanding), [[5]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/latin#lat-aquinas-de-veritate-intus-legere). A
  15th-century dictionary, the *Vocabularius breviloquus*, gives both *intus legere* and "ab inter et lego" in one entry [[6]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/latin#lat-breviloquus-intelligo-both-etymologies). A Basel treatise
  adds a third, punning one: *intelligentia* is "the bed of reason" (*lectus rationis*), where reason rests after disputing
  [[7]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/latin#lat-dicta-intelligentia-lectus-rationis). **Vico** rejects both standard readings. He takes *inter* as an intensive ("increase or
  perfection") [[8]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/early-modern#em-vico-intellegere-interlego-intensive). We found no ancient source for "choose between".
- **The ladder.** Boethius ranks sense, imagination, reason and intelligence, and gives *intelligentia* to the divine
  alone [[9]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/latin#lat-boethius-four-powers), [[10]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/latin#lat-boethius-ratio-human-intelligentia-divine). The pseudo-Augustinian *De spiritu et
  anima* adds *intellectus* below it: the soul is like the firmament through intellect and "like God through intelligence".
  It sets intellect beside the Thrones and intelligence beside the Cherubim [[11]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/latin#lat-despiritu-ladder-sensus-intelligentia). A manuscript in the Laurenziana
  gives intellect the created and intelligence the uncreated [[12]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/latin#lat-ms-ladder-intelligentia-increatum). Aquinas, against
  this, makes *intelligentia* only the *act* of the one intellect, not a power of its own [[13]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/latin#lat-aquinas-intelligentia-act-of-intellect),
  consistent with his view that understanding and reasoning are one power [[14]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/latin#lat-aquinas-same-power).
- **Into English** through Boethius. Chaucer's *Boece* has "wit, imaginacioun, resoun, intelligence", and
  "intelligence is only [to] the devyne nature" [[15]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/latin#lat-chaucer-boece-intelligence). One of the earliest English uses of
  the word for a faculty is for the faculty humans do *not* have.

## 2. A mind that moves a heaven (Aristotle to Dante)

- **Aristotle** posits as many unmoved "essences and principles" as there are spheres (55, or 47)
  [[16]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/greek#grk-aristotle-lambda8-movers-per-sphere). He does not use the word "intelligences". It comes through the Arabic and the Latin
  *Liber de causis*: "Omnis intelligentia plena est formis" [[17]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/latin#lat-liber-de-causis-intelligentia-plena-formis).
- **The Arabic chain.** For al-Fārābī, each intellect thinks the First and itself, and from these two acts come a sphere and the next intellect
  [[18]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/islamic#isl-farabi-chain-of-intellects-spheres). Avicenna, as Contarini reports him, has three products at each step (intellect, soul, sphere)
  [[19]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/latin#lat-contarini-avicenna-emanation-triad). Maimonides counts ten, the tenth being the Active Intellect [[20]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/jewish#jew-maimonides-active-intellect-tenth).
- **Intelligences are angels.** Al-Ghazālī already reports that the philosophers map the heavenly angels onto the celestial souls and the
  cherubim onto the pure intelligences [[21]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/islamic#isl-ghazali-philosophers-angels-are-souls). In Aquinas the separate substances
  "we call angels" are *intelligentiae* in books translated from the Arabic, "perhaps because such substances always
  understand in act" [[22]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/latin#lat-aquinas-intelligentiae-semper-actu-brentano), and all bodies are governed through angels
  [[23]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/latin#lat-aquinas-st-110-bodies-ruled-by-angels). Dante: the movers are "intelligenze, le quali la volgare gente chiama
  Angeli" [[24]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/latin#lat-dante-convivio-intelligenze-angeli); Plato's ideas were intelligences too [[25]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/latin#lat-dante-convivio-plato-ideas-intelligences);
  the angels move the Moon's heaven out of love [[26]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/latin#lat-dante-convivio-moon-movers-angels); the fallen are "intelligences in exile"
  [[27]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/latin#lat-dante-convivio-intelligenze-angels); and in *Paradiso* II "the intelligence" unfolds its goodness through the stars
  [[28]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/latin#lat-dante-paradiso-beati-motor-intelligenza). The *Vita nova*'s "intelligenza nova" draws the sigh beyond the outermost sphere
  [[29]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/latin#lat-dante-vita-nova-intelligenza-nova); whether it is a celestial Intelligence or a new understanding is open until Dante's prose gloss is read.
- **How it differs from us.** The angel does not reason. Its light is "a pure and most clear mirror", and it sees at once what we
  reach by discourse [[30]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/latin#lat-aquinas-angel-not-discursive-mirror). Above even that, God is *superintelligibilis*
  [[31]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/latin#lat-hersent-superintelligibilis): the oldest "super-" in this vocabulary is the one that is *beyond* intelligence.

## 3. An operable spirit (Agrippa)

- Agrippa's planetary magic squares each carry "an intelligence for good and a daemon for evil": Saturn's Agiel and Zazel
  each come to 45, the sum of the three-by-three square, and Jupiter's Iophiel and Hismael each to 136
  [[32]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/latin#lat-agrippa-planetary-tables-intelligence-daemon). Material numbers act only as they are "ruled and informed by the
  intelligences" [[33]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/latin#lat-agrippa-intelligences-rule-formal-numbers). In Agrippa the celestial mover has become an entity with a name, a number and a seal, paired
  with a daemon, and the magus can address it. This joins the magic study's mathematics-as-intermediate thread (Magic [[1]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/renaissance#math-agrippa-numbers-formal-virtue), `math-agrippa-mathematics-necessary-magic`, `grim-fourth-book-planetary-names`).

## 4. From minds to forces, and the Intelligences become "spirits" (Kepler, Locke)

- Kepler sets out Aristotle's case for immaterial movers with understanding and will [[34]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/early-modern#em-kepler-separate-minds-ministers),
  replaces them with a moving power that spreads out like light [[35]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/early-modern#em-kepler-virtus-motrix-like-light), and in 1621 writes:
  put *vim* for *anima* and you have my celestial physics. He says he once believed in souls, "steeped in Scaliger's doctrine *de motricibus
  intelligentiis*" [[36]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/early-modern#em-kepler-anima-to-vis-1621). With that the Intelligences lose their job of moving the heavens.
- They survive only as a class of being. Locke's "FINITE INTELLIGENCES" stand between God and bodies. Locke calls the faculty
  "understanding" [[37]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/early-modern#em-locke-intelligences-are-spirits). Kant's *Intelligenz* is a standpoint, the self regarded as a member of the world of understanding
  [[38]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/modern-phil#mph-kant-sich-als-intelligenz), [[39]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/modern-phil#mph-kant-spontaneity-intelligenz-b158). It is not something one has more or less of.

## 5. Information (Shakespeare to the newsbooks)

- In *Macbeth* "this strange intelligence" is news [[40]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/early-modern#em-macbeth-strange-intelligence). In *Leviathan* every one of the
  word's three uses means news or espionage, never a power of the mind [[41]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/early-modern#em-hobbes-intelligence-is-news). The graded,
  comparative ability is "Witte" [[42]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/early-modern#em-hobbes-wit-ranked-virtue).
- Writers on war, diplomacy and the state made secret intelligence a formal part of government [[43]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/early-modern#em-secret-intelligences-statecraft). Hartlib's network dealt in handwritten news
  [[44]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/early-modern#em-hartlib-paid-correspondent), and his circle called the newsbooks "Mercuries" [[45]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/early-modern#em-plattes-mercuries-newsbooks).
- The two senses meet in Hermes. Everard's 1650 *Pymander* calls him "The thrice greatest Intelligencer", the first to pass on knowledge in writing,
  and Barrett's *Magus* (1801) is subtitled *The Celestial Intelligencer* [[46]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/hermetic#her-everard-hermes-first-intelligencer).

## 6. A measured quantity (Galton to Boring)

- Galton's word is "ability" or "genius". "Intelligence" is rare in him and mostly applied to animals and races [[47]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/cogsci#cog-galton-ability-genius-not-intelligence).
  Danziger argues that intelligence was first applied to humans in its modern psychological form in 1904 [[48]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/cogsci#cog-danziger-intelligence-1904), the
  year of Spearman's "General Intelligence" [[49]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/cogsci#cog-spearman-g). Binet's faculty was judgment [[50]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/cogsci#cog-binet-judgment).
- Stern's 1912 *Intelligenzquotient* is a ratio of mental age to life age, made to say what fraction of normal intelligence a
  feeble-minded child has [[51]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/cogsci#cog-stern-intelligenzquotient-1912). Boring's "Intelligence is what the tests test" comes with a
  concession: a more technical term would have been better, "the damage is done" [[52]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/cogsci#cog-boring-tests-test-damage-done),
  [[53]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/cogsci#cog-boring-what-tests-test). Goodey treats the whole concept as historically contingent [[54]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/critique#crit-goodey-intelligence-contingent).

## 7. An artifact (Turing to Bostrom)

- Turing's paper has "Intelligence" in its title, but its body asks whether machines can *think* [[55]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/ai#ai-turing-intelligence-word-only-title), [[56]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/ai#ai-turing-imitation).
  The Dartmouth proposal (1955) uses "artificial intelligence" in its first sentence, on the conjecture that every feature of intelligence can be described
  well enough for a machine to simulate it [[57]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/ai#ai-dartmouth-artificial-intelligence-phrase). This is the measured, describable sense of section 6.
- Good's "ultraintelligent machine" and "the last invention" [[58]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/ai#ai-good-ultraintelligent-last-invention); Vinge's
  "superhuman intelligence" [[59]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/ai#ai-vinge-superhuman-intelligence); Bostrom's "a superintelligence" defined as "an intellect"
  that companies are not [[60]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/ai#ai-bostrom-1998-superintelligence-an-intellect). The definers handle the ordinary word through
  dictionaries and never through its history [[61]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/ai#ai-defs-dictionary-sense-no-etymology), [[62]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/ai#ai-legg-hutter-universal), [[63]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/ai#ai-chollet-skill-acquisition).

## What survives in "artificial intelligence" and "superintelligence"

| Sense | Period | Survives in AI? |
|---|---|---|
| act of the highest faculty (*intus legere*) | antiquity–1500 | not in the definers we read |
| a separate mind / angel ("an intelligence") | 1100–1700 | **the grammar of "a superintelligence"**: a mind as an entity, ranked above humans |
| an operable spirit with a name and a number | Agrippa | in the magic-kb analogy of the summoned servant, not in the word itself |
| information, news, espionage | 1590–today | in "intelligence agency"; not in AI |
| a measured quantity | 1904– | **the content of "artificial intelligence"** (Dartmouth's "described precisely") |
| an artifact | 1955– | itself |

- **Reading.** The founding texts do not mention angels, the Intelligences or Dionysius. The scholarship that puts angels beside AI
  argues by analogy [[64]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/ai#ai-scholarship-aquinas-angels-ai-analogy), or against the analogy [[65]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/critique#crit-ai-chua-angel-computer-gap). Geraci links AI to
  apocalypticism, not to angelology [[66]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/ai#ai-geraci-apocalyptic-ai). So the old sense carries over at most in grammar and in rank, and its content is inverted.
  The medieval higher intelligence does not reason, and the modern one reasons better [[67]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/ai#ai-interp-superintelligence-no-medieval-descent).
  This is a low-confidence reading. It rests partly on abstracts, and Good 1965 and Bostrom 2014 were not read in full.
- **Against the thesis (ideas/06).** At no point does the word mean "harmonizing". Its highest senses are intuitive vision (the angel's
  mirror), moving a heaven, and information. The nearest thing to integration is Kant's spontaneity of combination
  [[39]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/modern-phil#mph-kant-spontaneity-intelligenz-b158), and that is the understanding's work, not a rank.

## Open questions

- When does English "intelligence" first mean an *ability someone has more of* (between Hobbes's "wit" and Spearman)? We have not read 18th–19th-century
  English usage. Candidates: Hume, Reid, Spencer's *Principles of Psychology* (1855), and the "intelligence" of animals in Romanes.
- Is the *inter-legere* "choose between" reading medieval or modern? The earliest place we found it is the *Breviloquus* (15th c.).
- Do the Latin Dionysius translations themselves use *superintelligibilis*, or only Hersent (1626)?
- Good 1965 is cited only as Vinge quotes it. Read the original (Advances in Computers 6) and Bostrom 2014.

title: Words for mind and intelligence across the traditions
md:
**Purpose.** To help a writer say which word they mean, and to catch an English "intellect", "mind" or "intelligence" that is hiding a different native word. Each term has one page-cited use from a primary text Source Library holds, given as a double-bracketed claim id. The claim carries the quote, the page link and, usually, the original wording. **Not held** means no Source Library primary text for that term was found when this lexicon was built (2026-10-24); the gap is an acquisition or transcription target. Glosses marked **(GK)** are general knowledge of the language and were not read on a page in this pass.

**Reading the table.** *Conception* uses the KB's `levels` vocabulary: **faculty** (a power of a soul), **cosmic** (a principle of the world), **divine** (an attribute or hypostasis of God), **skill** (a measurable ability), **collective** (shared by many), **machine**, **ethical** (bound up with the good).

## Greek

| Term | Root sense / gloss | Conception | Page-cited use | Held |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| νοῦς *nous* | mind, intellect; the power that grasps (GK: from *noein*, to perceive or think) | cosmic (Anaxagoras), faculty, divine | Anaxagoras: nous alone is "mixed with nothing" and rules all things [[1]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/greek#grk-anaxagoras-nous-unmixed); nous orders all things [[2]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/greek#grk-anaxagoras-nous-arranges) | yes (Diels) |
| νόησις *noēsis* | intellection, the top state of the divided line | faculty | Plato, *Rep.* VI 511d [[3]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/greek#grk-plato-divided-line); Aristotle's self-thinking thought, νόησις νοήσεως [[4]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/greek#grk-aristotle-noesis-noeseos) | yes |
| διάνοια *dianoia* | discursive thought, thinking-through | faculty | *Rep.* VI 511d, second section of the line [[3]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/greek#grk-plato-divided-line); Iamblichus' *dianoēta* vs *noēta* [[5]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/greek#grk-iamblichus-dianoeta-noeta) | yes |
| λόγος *logos* | account, word, reason, ratio | cosmic, collective | Heraclitus: the logos is common (ξυνός) but most live as if with a private understanding [[6]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/greek#grk-heraclitus-logos-common) | yes (Fairbanks) |
| φρόνησις *phronēsis* | practical wisdom | faculty, ethical | Aristotle *NE* VI: a true practical state about what is good for a human [[7]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/greek#grk-aristotle-phronesis-def); impossible without being good [[8]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/greek#grk-aristotle-phronesis-requires-goodness) | yes |
| σοφία *sophia* | wisdom; the most precise knowing | faculty | *NE* VI.7: sophia is nous plus epistēmē of the highest things [[9]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/greek#grk-aristotle-sophia) | yes |
| ἐπιστήμη *epistēmē* | scientific knowledge, demonstration | faculty | *NE* VI.3, one of the five states by which the soul attains truth [[10]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/greek#grk-aristotle-ne-five-states) | yes |
| Neoplatonic Νοῦς | the second hypostasis: intellect identical with its objects | divine, cosmic | Plotinus *Enn.* V.3: intellect, intellection and intelligible are one [[11]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/greek#grk-plotinus-intellect-identity); Proclus *ET* 167: every intellect thinks itself [[12]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/greek#grk-proclus-every-intellect-self) | yes, but Plotinus in Taylor's English only |

## Hermetic

| Term | Gloss | Conception | Page-cited use | Held |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ὁ τῆς αὐθεντίας νοῦς | "the Nous of the Sovereignty", Poimandres' self-name | divine | CH I.2 [[13]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/hermetic#her-poimandres-nous-of-sovereignty); Ficino's Latin *mens divinae potentiae* [[14]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/hermetic#her-ficino-pimander-mens-divinae-potentiae) | yes (Scott, Ficino) |
| νοῦς vs λόγος (CH IV) | nous is a gift, logos is given to all | divine, faculty (of some) | God gave logos to all humans but not nous [[15]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/hermetic#her-ch4-logos-to-all-nous-not); the krater of nous set as a prize [[16]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/hermetic#her-ch4-krater-prize) | yes |
| νοῦς ἐν ἀνθρώποις θεός | "in men this nous is god" | divine | CH XII.1 [[17]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/hermetic#her-ch12-nous-substance-of-god) | yes (rests on the Greek; Scott's English leaves a gap) |

## Latin

| Term | Gloss | Conception | Page-cited use | Held |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| *intellectus* | understanding; simple grasp of truth | faculty | Aquinas *ST* I q.79 a.8: reasoning is to understanding as motion to rest [[18]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/latin#lat-aquinas-ratio-motion-intellectus-rest); Eriugena maps νοῦς to *intellectus* [[19]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/latin#lat-eriugena-intellectus-ratio-sensus) | yes |
| *intelligentia* | the highest cognitive power; in Boethius, divine | divine, faculty | Boethius *Cons.* V: reason is human, intelligence divine [[20]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/latin#lat-boethius-ratio-human-intelligentia-divine); Augustine's memory, intelligence, will [[21]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/latin#lat-augustine-memoria-intelligentia-voluntas) | yes (Boethius in English only) |

| *ratio* | reason, reckoning, discursive thought | faculty | Aquinas: *ratiocinari* proceeds from one thing understood to another [[24]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/latin#lat-aquinas-same-power) | yes |
| *ingenium* | wit, native talent, inventiveness | skill | Augustine: a child's ingenium judged by memory, understanding and zeal [[25]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/latin#lat-augustine-ingenium-measured); Isidore: nothing more excellent than ingenium [[26]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/latin#lat-isidore-ingenium) | yes |

## Arabic (and its Latin)

| Term | Gloss | Conception | Page-cited use | Held |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| عقل *ʿaql* | intellect; (GK) root sense "to bind, restrain" | faculty, cosmic | Al-Kindī's four intellects (Latin) [[27]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/islamic#isl-kindi-four-intellects); the editor's Arabic terms [[28]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/islamic#isl-kindi-terms-editor); Ibn Ṭufayl's *al-maʿqūl* and *al-manqūl* agree [[29]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/islamic#isl-ibntufayl-reason-tradition-agree) | indirect: Arabic script only in an editor's gloss and in Ibn Ṭufayl |
| al-ʿaql al-faʿʿāl / *intelligentia agens* | the agent (active) intellect, separate, always in act | cosmic, collective | Avicenna: it is to the soul as the sun to sight [[30]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/islamic#isl-avicenna-agent-intelligence-sun); learning is aptitude to be joined to it [[31]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/islamic#isl-avicenna-learning-conjunction); al-Fārābī's "schaffender Intellect" [[32]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/islamic#isl-farabi-active-intellect-ray) | yes (Latin Avicenna; Dieterici's German al-Fārābī) |
| material / possible intellect | the receptive intellect; one for all in Averroes | collective | Averroes as quoted by Brentano [[33]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/islamic#isl-averroes-one-material-intellect); Aquinas' reply [[34]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/critique#crit-islamic-aquinas-one-understands) | **Averroes' Long Commentary not held**: cited only second-hand |

## Hebrew

| Term | Gloss | Conception | Page-cited use | Held |

## The distinctions the words force

1. **Intellect vs reasoning.** Almost every literate tradition here has a pair: νοῦς/διάνοια, *intellectus*/*ratio*, buddhi/manas, prajñā/reasoning, *Vernunft*/*Verstand*. The upper term is usually the grasp and the lower the process. Kant reverses the valence: for him *Vernunft* is higher, but its ideas only regulate (`ideas/02`).
2. **Faculty vs principle.** νοῦς, the agent intellect, Bruno's *intelletto universale* and Hegel's *Geist* name something outside or above any one person; *ingenium*, buddhi and *g* name something a person has more or less of (`ideas/01`).
3. **Gift vs endowment.** In the Hermetica logos is given to all and nous is not [[15]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/hermetic#her-ch4-logos-to-all-nous-not); in Cusanus every mind is a living image of God [[75]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/latin#lat-cusanus-mens-living-image); in Mencius every person has the sprout of zhi [[62]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/chinese#chn-mencius-shifei-sprout-of-zhi) (`ideas/03`).
4. **Knowing vs being good.** φρόνησις and 智 carry the good inside them; *ratio* in Hobbes and "intelligence" in Burt and Bostrom are stripped of it (`ideas/04`).
5. **Awareness vs intelligence.** Sāṃkhya separates the deciding buddhi from the witnessing puruṣa [[48]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/indian#ind-sankhya-split); *rig pa* is awareness, not cleverness [[69]](/explore/histories/nous/claims/tibetan#tib-pemalingpa-rigpa-own-forms) (`ideas/05`).

title: Schools and lineages of mind
md:
**What this page is.** It shows who learned from whom and who answered whom, and it groups the authors into schools by what they took intelligence to be. Every solid edge rests on a claim in which one text names, quotes or translates the other. A dotted edge is a connection that was *not* verified on a page: general knowledge, or a parallel with no transmission shown. The grouping is a judgement, not a standard taxonomy. The dated list is in `timeline.md`. **The short version.** There are five schools, and they sort by where they put the mind. (1) **Mind above the world**, ordering it while unmixed: Anaxagoras, Aristotle's god, Plotinus, Proclus. (2) **One mind outside us that we join**: the agent intellect from al-Kindī to Avicenna, Maimonides and the Latin debate. (3) **Mind as image**: the Hermetica, Philo, Maimonides, Cusanus, where the human mind is an image of the divine, given to some or to all. (4) **Mind as ruler of the person**: Philo's ἡγεμών, Xunzi's lord of the body, the Katha charioteer, Aquinas' will-king. (5) **Mind as tool or quantity**: Hobbes, Leibniz's *calculemus*, Galton, Spearman, Bostrom. A sixth current refuses the frame: **Daoist and Buddhist emptying**, where the highest knowing is reached by giving up *zhi*, stilling citta, or recognising *rig pa*. The Chinese and Indian lines have no verified edge to the Greek line. Where they converge on intellect vs reason, it is convergence, not transmission. ## The lineage diagram Arrows run forward in time. **quotes / translates** means the later text names, quotes or translates the earlier one on the page we cite. **answers** means it argues against it on the page.
